a39d0049d071: The Federal Assembly is bicameral. The Federation Council is the chamber of the regions: one senator each from the legislative and executive bodies of every federal subject (plus up to 30 representatives appointed by the president, and life senators who are former presidents); its chair is Valentina Matviyenko. It approves or rejects Duma laws; a rejected law can be passed again by the Duma with two-thirds of the votes (300 of 450). President Vladimir Putin (elected in 2024 until 2030) may impose a veto, which is overridden by two-thirds of the total number of Duma deputies and senators (Art. 107). Federal constitutional laws are passed by 3/4 of the Federation Council and 2/3 of the Duma, with no veto (Art. 108). Amendments to Chapters 3–8 of the Constitution require 3/4 of the Federation Council, 2/3 of the Duma and approval by the legislatures of 2/3 of the federal subjects. The game counts 170 seats from 85 subjects and 30 presidential representatives (who vote with the government), 200 in total; senators from Ukrainian territory under Russian control (Crimea, Sevastopol and 4 oblasts, whose annexation most countries do not recognise) are not counted.
